hypothesis: The current MAP01 v15 event and scorer files contain enough same-runtime timestamp and intent-ID data to classify an independently scored positive change after a recovery's accepted timestamp, a post-acceptance/pre-first-input baseline, and a bounded post-input positive sample.
test: One deterministic CPU-only file-level construction experiment with seven JSONL fixtures matching current ExecutorV13, input-owner-v12, scorer-file-sink-v1, and independent-progress-clock-v2 records.
decision_gate: PASS only if the valid fixture joins one accepted id to its first input admission and reports an admission-bracketed useful score change using the latest pre-input baseline; pre-input-only progress, missing baseline, missed scorer period, malformed sample receipt, and absent/ambiguous intent identity all fail closed.
missed_period_rule: Any missed scheduled sample period from the selected baseline through the positive sample rejects classification.
clock_rule: All event and scorer times are synthetic values in one runtime perf_counter_ns domain. Runtime source code presently calls perf_counter_ns for accepted_ns, admitted_ns, and ProgressSample.sample_ns; this construction test does not verify a live episode or host-clock conversion.
resources: CPU-only deterministic test in a fresh OrbStack linux/arm64 python:3.12-slim container; no game, model, live input, GPU, WSLc, or formal allocation.
claim_limit: Admission-bracketed progress is an observed interval association only. It does not establish exact effect time, causality, recovery efficacy, or MAP01 completion.
